questions.explanation: This is the same shape-versus-substance gap that runs through the phase — fluency isn't evidence of soundness, and reasoning quality doesn't shift accountability away from the human who has to answer for the decision.

questions.from: Previous module — Agreement and Flattery
questions.prompt: Why is the pull toward agreement weakest on hard, checkable facts and strongest on judgment calls?

options.label: A hard fact has a near-universally agreed answer in training data that resists the learned agreement tendency; a judgment call has no such anchor, leaving more room for the tendency to dominate
The model has a specific rule that applies only to arithmetic questions
This isn't actually a real pattern

questions.explanation: From Agreement and Flattery: sycophancy operates on a gradient tied to how strongly a checkable ground truth exists — clear facts resist it, judgment calls leave the most room for it.

questions.from: Previous module — Agreement and Flattery
questions.prompt: Why does “give me the strongest argument against this” tend to produce more genuine pushback than “please be honest with me”?

options.label: “Be honest” asks for a disposition satisfiable by tone alone; the counter-argument request asks for specific content that agreement cannot fulfill
The two instructions are functionally identical in practice
“Be honest” is actually the more reliably effective phrasing

questions.explanation: From Agreement and Flattery: a content-based request forces the model to produce a specific deliverable that validation can't substitute for, unlike a disposition request.

questions.from: Previous module — Agreement and Flattery
questions.prompt: Why is repeatedly rephrasing a personal decision until the answer feels right described as building an echo chamber?

options.label: It combines a no-ground-truth judgment call with the freedom to iterate toward a preferred framing, letting someone unconsciously fish for validation while experiencing it as independent advice
The model has no stake in the outcome, so every answer it gives is automatically independent of how it was asked
This isn't actually a real risk for personal decisions

questions.explanation: From Agreement and Flattery: having no stake doesn't make an answer independent of framing, and iterative rephrasing on a ground-truth-free topic compounds the agreement pull into a self-built echo chamber.

questions.from: Previous module — Agreement and Flattery
questions.prompt: What makes a counter-argument genuinely specific rather than performative?

options.label: It references something particular to the actual plan or decision — a specific number or assumption — rather than a generic caveat that could be pasted into a critique of any plan unchanged
Its length — longer counter-arguments are always more genuine
Whether it uses the word "risk" at least once

questions.explanation: From Agreement and Flattery: the pasted-into-any-plan test is the tell — a genuine counter-argument engages with something specific to your actual numbers or details.

questions.from: Older module — Fabrication
questions.prompt: Which question shape reliably raises fabrication risk, independent of topic?

options.label: A fixed enumeration quota, like “list six examples,” when fewer genuine ones may exist
Any question about a well-known scientific constant
Any question phrased as a complete, polite sentence

questions.explanation: From Fabrication: a fixed quota pushes the model to fill every slot whether or not that many genuine examples are well represented, producing invented items past the real ones.

questions.from: Older module — Verifying Efficiently
questions.prompt: What should actually determine how much verification effort an AI-assisted task gets?

options.label: What being wrong would actually cost — irreversibility, who's affected, and how far the answer reaches
How confident the AI's tone sounded when it answered
How long or detailed the AI's answer was

questions.explanation: From Verifying Efficiently: tone and length carry no information about real-world stakes — the legitimate factors are irreversibility, who's affected, and reach.
